title: Funciones, contratos y descomposición
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned.

roadmap_expectation.T1: function definition, call, return, positional/keyword parameters and safe defaults
roadmap_expectation.T2: pre/postconditions, docstrings, gradual type hints and domain errors
roadmap_expectation.T3: small functions, composition, purity, effects and I/O injection
roadmap_expectation.T4: LEGB, basic closures, executable examples and behavior-preserving refactor

later_boundaries.S06: lists, tuples, dicts, sets, slicing, unpacking
later_boundaries.S07: string methods and Unicode mental model

live_site.note: Public fetch remained blocked in this environment. No exact hydrated-render parity claim is made.

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: The learner is meeting functions for the first legitimate time, but the first examples hide definition/call/return semantics behind unearned string methods, mutable lists, exceptions and structured result containers.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: S06 collection mutation and S09 exception flow, plus S07 string-method mechanics.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: That keeping the same function signature means the implementation may change freely, even if its documented guarantees change.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The caption says implementation is inside the box and 'Cambiar el cuerpo sin tocar los bordes es libre'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: This is the learner's first legitimate function-contract lesson.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A function contract includes behavioral guarantees, not only the visible signature or input/output shape. Internal code can change without changing the signature and still violate the postcondition.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can believe that any body-only change is a safe refactor as long as the parameters and return shape stay unchanged.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Change the caption to say the implementation may change only while preserving the contract: preconditions, outputs, errors and observable effects.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The first worked function uses raw.strip().split(), join(), title(), annotations and a second no-return function while string methods are formally S07 and function mechanics are new here.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner can use basic values, decisions and loops but has not earned the string-method toolkit.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The example intended to teach definition/call/return requires the learner to decode several unrelated transformations before they can trace the function boundary.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can reproduce normalize_nombre while still being unable to explain when a def body runs, how raw receives an argument or how return hands a value back.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Start T1-A with a one-operation function whose body uses already-earned syntax, trace definition -> call -> parameter binding -> return, then introduce normalize_nombre after the function model exists.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The key safe-default outcome is taught using [] lists, append(), shared-object mutation and list-return behavior although S06 is the first collection lesson and the prior ledger does not credit list mutation mastery.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No operational list/dict mutation model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The roadmap requires safe defaults before it teaches the mutable structures that make the default bug understandable; the lesson uses those structures without a bounded micro-model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can memorize 'use None' without understanding that one mutable default object is created once and then changed across calls.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add an explicit micro-model: a list is a changeable container; the default object is created once at def time; append changes that same object. Keep the detailed collection mechanics for S06.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The rule is repeatedly phrased as 'nunca una lista o un diccionario' / 'nunca uses lista/dict mutable como default'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is forming the reusable rule for safe defaults.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The real hazard is a mutable default that the function mutates; lists and dicts are examples, not the complete category. Mutable class instances can create the same problem.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can conclude that a set or other mutable object is automatically safe merely because it is not a list or dict.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say 'evita objetos mutables como listas o diccionarios cuando la función puede modificarlos; usa None y crea un objeto nuevo dentro'.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Immediately after first defining call/return, the lesson introduces first-class functions, storing them in lists, returning functions and callbacks.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is still constructing the first function-call model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: These are true facts but they are not needed for the T1-A outcome and introduce future collection/callback concepts before the basic call trace is stable.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can spend working memory on what a callback or function-as-value is instead of distinguishing definition, call and return.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Move first-class/callback material to T4-A when closures/factories are introduced, or to an optional note after the core function model.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Prose defines a precondition as what must be true before calling; the figure says the precondition 'se comprueba antes de tocar nada'; the example states 'Pre: raw es str' but performs no explicit type check and would raise AttributeError for None/int.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No prior formal design-by-contract model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson does not distinguish an assumed caller obligation from a runtime validation performed by the callee or by an external boundary.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner cannot tell whether every documented precondition must be checked inside the function, is automatically enforced by Python, or is merely required of callers.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one sentence: a precondition states what callers must provide; it may be assumed inside trusted core code or explicitly validated at an untrusted boundary. Make the figure say 'declarar/validar según el boundary', not that every precondition is automatically checked.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The callout says 'Si el docstring y el código discrepan, gana el código'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is being taught that a docstring expresses a contract.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Runtime behavior comes from code, but intended contract is not automatically whatever the current implementation happens to do. A mismatch is a defect that requires deciding which artifact is wrong.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can silently rewrite documentation to match a buggy implementation instead of treating the discrepancy as evidence requiring resolution.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Replace with 'si discrepan, hay un defecto: ejecuta/consulta la especificación y corrige el artefacto que no representa la política acordada'.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says not to overload S05 with advanced generics, then immediately imports Optional and Tuple and uses Tuple[bool, Optional[int], Optional[str]], a three-field tuple result, before S06 teaches tuples and structured collections.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Simple annotations such as x: str -> str only.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The worked example violates the section's own gradual-hints rule and makes type syntax plus tuple semantics prerequisites for understanding domain errors.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can interpret type hints as a nested mini-language they must master immediately and cannot distinguish the function's domain-error idea from its result-container syntax.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Keep T2-B examples to simple public annotations such as raw: str -> str; postpone Optional/Tuple result protocols to S06 or introduce one bounded str | None form only when it is genuinely needed.

confirmed_findings.evidence: normalize_email raises ValueError and theory demonstrates try/except; parse_edad also uses try/except, while the roadmap reserves exception/recovery mechanics for S09.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No usable exception-flow model from the effective ledger.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: S05 legitimately needs to state domain-error behavior, but it asks the learner to trace exception control flow without first teaching what raise interrupts, what except catches, or where execution resumes.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can memorize try/except as boilerplate around validation without understanding why the normal return path is skipped.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either give a tightly bounded micro-model of raise/ValueError sufficient for function contracts and defer recovery patterns to S09, or use explicit result values in S05 and postpone try/except demonstrations.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The callout prescribes 'raise para API internas puras; tupla u objeto de resultado cuando el lote no debe abortar'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is choosing an error contract for the first time.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Purity does not determine whether errors should be exceptions or result values, and a batch can catch per-record exceptions without aborting the whole batch.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can infer a false one-to-one rule between internal/pure functions and exceptions, then design inconsistent APIs when callers have different recovery needs.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State that either pattern can be valid; choose one explicit contract based on how callers must recover, and use it consistently within the module.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The canonical composition example returns a dict from normalize_record, constructs a dict literal and uses that container as the core representation before S06 teaches dictionaries.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No usable dict model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner must understand a future data structure to see what the orchestrator returns and how composition preserves each helper's result.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can understand each helper separately but lose the composition model exactly when the outputs are packaged in unexplained dict syntax.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Demonstrate composition first with a simple returned string/value pair expressed separately; introduce record dictionaries only after S06 or provide a bounded explicit preview if the roadmap is revised.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: learning outcome 'inyectar I/O en el borde' + S05-T3-B
confirmed_findings.evidence: T3-B explains that I/O belongs at the boundary, but the promised injection example passes a normalizer function as norm=normalize_telefono and the callout calls that 'inyección'; it does not inject any input/output dependency.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Functions are now in scope; I/O separation is a declared outcome.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson conflates injecting a transformation strategy with injecting I/O and never shows how external reading/writing is supplied to or kept outside the pure core.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can finish S05 believing that passing any function argument counts as I/O injection and still hard-code open()/print() around business logic.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either rename the outcome/topic to dependency injection if that is the intended skill, or show one tiny boundary function that receives an I/O callable while the normalizer remains pure.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The main idempotence example computes digits with ''.join(ch for ch in raw if ch.isdigit()), combining a generator expression and string-method semantics that have not been taught as usable concepts.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic for loops are usable; generator expressions and string-method validation are not.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The example intended to make f(f(x)) == f(x) visible hides the transformation behind new syntax and new text rules.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner may verify the printed equality but be unable to predict why the first normalization produced that value or whether applying it twice should remain stable.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Demonstrate idempotence first with a normalizer whose transformation is already transparent to the learner; move generator-expression/string-method implementation to the later text lesson.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The callout introduces lambda syntax while the section's own function model and dependency-injection idea are still being learned.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Named def functions only.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Lambda is not required for any S05 outcome and adds a second function syntax plus substitution semantics at the exact point where I/O injection is already underexplained.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can treat lambda as required for testing/injection or confuse it with a fundamentally different kind of function.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Remove lambda from core S05 theory or put it in an optional later note after closures/factories.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose presents make_phone_normalizer(prefix) as country-configurable, but the inner function hard-codes startswith('51') and d[2:] regardless of the supplied prefix. Execution with make_phone_normalizer('+1') duplicates +1 for an already +1 input and strips a leading 51 even though +1 was requested.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is using a closure to understand captured configuration.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The example claims configuration is captured by prefix but one major policy decision remains hidden and Peru-specific inside the closure.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can believe the factory is generic by country when changing the prefix alone does not change its country-code stripping logic.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use a closure example whose behavior depends only on the captured prefix, or pass the digits-to-strip/country policy explicitly as configuration too.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The closure example simultaneously uses isdigit(), startswith(), len(), slicing d[2:], nested defs and country normalization. Slicing is S06 and the text-method toolkit is S07.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner needs only enough syntax to see Local -> Enclosing -> Global -> Builtin and a captured prefix.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The closure mechanism is buried under unrelated phone-normalization rules.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can fail to identify which value is remembered by the closure because most visible lines are about text parsing rather than scope.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use a minimal factory such as make_prefixer(prefix) whose inner function returns prefix + raw, then trace raw/prefix/global separately.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The file defines normalize_email v1, defines _examples, then redefines normalize_email v2 and calls _examples only afterward. Python resolves the global normalize_email when _examples executes, so every assertion runs against v2; v1 is never tested in that run.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is supposed to see tests fixed before and after a refactor.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The worked example does not establish a pre-refactor green baseline and therefore cannot demonstrate that behavior was preserved across the change.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can believe tests prove a refactor preserved behavior even when only the final implementation was ever exercised.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Run the same example assertions before redefining/refactoring the function and again afterward, or keep v1/v2 under distinct names and compare both against the same examples.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The paragraph says that if asserts stay green, 'la conducta se preservó'. Paragraph 5 later correctly limits this by saying green proves only what the examples cover.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner is forming a first model of regression evidence.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The strong earlier statement is broader than the evidence and is only corrected several paragraphs later.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can temporarily form the rule 'all green examples prove unchanged behavior', overlooking uncovered inputs or side effects.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Change the first statement to 'si siguen verdes, preservaste la conducta que esos ejemplos cubren'; keep the later caveat.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: opening callout/optional criterion + T3-A canonical orchestrator
confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson says closing S05 means four normalizers plus an orchestrator with docstring/hints/idempotence demonstrated, but theory's normalize_record combines only nombre/email and has no docstring; normalize_direccion is never implemented in a theory code block.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Theory should give enough canonical evidence before practice, without having to inspect You Do.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner sees the delivery contract but not a complete learner-facing model of that contract inside theory.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can reach practice knowing the names of four policies but without a canonical example showing the full orchestrator boundary promised by the lesson.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either narrow the theory callout to the patterns actually modeled, or add one compact final reference example of the four-function orchestrator after the concepts have been taught.

confirmed_findings.evidence: S05 promotes assert as executable examples but does not locally remind learners that Python -O removes assert statements; prior S03 testing knowledge was not credited as USABLE.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No stable testing/assert mental model.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Assert is shown as evidence for refactoring without delimiting it as a development/example mechanism rather than production validation.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can reuse assert as the only enforcement of a business precondition and assume it always executes.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add a one-sentence boundary: asserts are development checks/examples and can be removed under python -O; do not use them as the only production validation of external input.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: tagline, callouts, optional contract and multiple theory paragraphs
confirmed_findings.evidence: CP-N1-B and CASO-LIM-005 remain learner-facing internal identifiers without stable first-use expansion in plain language.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No institutional identifier vocabulary beyond what each lesson explicitly teaches.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner is repeatedly asked to treat internal codes as meaningful nouns.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can recognize the labels but not explain whether they denote a project, gate, dataset, exercise or software component.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Expand each at first use, e.g. 'CP-N1-B, el segundo incremento del proyecto acumulativo de Nivel 1' and 'CASO-LIM-005, el caso sintético de normalización de esta sección'.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson uses placeholders params/args and then positional/keyword arguments, but never plainly distinguishes a parameter in the definition from an argument value supplied by a call.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No formal function vocabulary.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A core relation is left for inference at the moment parameter passing is introduced.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a learner can use 'parameter' and 'argument' as interchangeable labels and form an unstable model of how call values bind to function-local names.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add: 'parámetro = nombre declarado en def; argumento = valor que entregas al llamar; la llamada vincula cada argumento con un parámetro'.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Type hints are presented as runtime enforcement.
rejected_findings.reason: The theory explicitly says Python does not enforce annotations at runtime and distinguishes static checking from runtime validation.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The mutable-default behavior shown by bad_add is technically incorrect because the first call should print [1].
rejected_findings.reason: Function-call arguments to print are evaluated before print renders them; both returned references point at the same list, so the second mutation makes both display [1, 2]. Execution confirmed the stated output.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: PEP 257 does not support documenting arguments, return values and exceptions in function docstrings.
rejected_findings.reason: PEP 257 explicitly recommends that function/method docstrings summarize behavior and document arguments, return values, side effects, exceptions and restrictions when applicable.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: .title() is being sold as a production-safe universal human-name normalizer.
rejected_findings.reason: The opening explicitly warns that title() does not represent all real names and labels it a laboratory policy.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Idempotence is defined as a property every function must have.
rejected_findings.reason: The text applies f(f(x)) == f(x) specifically as the property required of the course's normalizers, not of arbitrary functions.
Nothing in the section requires that interpretation; deterministic exception behavior can coexist with a side-effect-free transformation contract.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The historical deep-research S05 report is usable evidence that Section 5 is missing.
rejected_findings.reason: The current canonical source is present and fully inspectable; the historical report did not have the current source and is superseded.

unresolved_questions.question: Does the hydrated live page render the same theory order, figures and callouts as this main-branch source?
Should S05 intentionally microteach mutable-container semantics for safe defaults, or should the detailed mutable-default example move after S06?
Should S05 intentionally microteach raise/ValueError as contract behavior while deferring try/except recovery to S09, or should exception-based examples be postponed?

element_inventory.current_content: Un registro puede viajar de un formulario de salud a un sistema de citas... Construyes un núcleo puro ... detrás de una CLI, un ETL o clases de dominio.
element_inventory.attack: CLI/ETL/core are future terms; might hide the mechanism.
element_inventory.defense: The actor/input/transformation outcome is mostly concrete and the later destinations are contextual, not prerequisites.
element_inventory.improved_content: Un registro puede pasar de un formulario a otro sistema y, en cada frontera, las mismas reglas de limpieza deben producir el mismo resultado. Aquí separas cada transformación en una función con una entrada, una regla y una salida explícitas. El núcleo solo transforma valores; la lectura de archivos, consola o red se conecta después en el borde del programa.

element_inventory.current_content: En S04 aprendiste a recorrer datos y resumir decisiones; ahora debes poner nombre y límites a esas decisiones... una promesa pequeña con una puerta de entrada, una regla interna y una salida...
element_inventory.attack: Analogy could imply all functions necessarily return a value.
element_inventory.defense: This section intentionally focuses normalizers that do return values and later discusses effects separately.
element_inventory.improved_content: En S04 aprendiste a recorrer datos y resumir decisiones; ahora debes poner nombre y límites a esas decisiones para no copiarlas por todo el programa. Una función no es una caja misteriosa: es una promesa pequeña con una puerta de entrada, una regla interna y una salida que otra pieza puede usar.

element_inventory.current_content: Esa promesa tiene un nombre técnico, contrato, y dos mitades... precondiciones... postcondiciones...
element_inventory.attack: Exceptional behavior is folded into postconditions and enforcement remains unclear.
element_inventory.defense: Core terms are defined causally; enforcement ambiguity is addressed as F06 in T2-A where it becomes operational.
element_inventory.improved_content: Ese acuerdo tiene un nombre técnico: contrato. Las precondiciones describen lo que quien llama debe proporcionar. Las postcondiciones describen lo que la función garantiza cuando cumple su ruta normal; el contrato también debe documentar los errores o excepciones que pueden ocurrir.

element_inventory.current_content: El contrato se vuelve verificable si la función es pura... misma entrada... misma salida... no toca disco, red ni imprime...
element_inventory.attack: Purity does not make a contract fully verifiable.
element_inventory.defense: The paragraph's causal point is testability and absence of effects; 'se vuelve verificable' is rhetorical but too absolute.
element_inventory.improved_content: La pureza hace más fácil comprobar ese contrato: con la misma entrada obtienes el mismo resultado y la función no modifica disco, red, consola ni estado externo por su cuenta. Así puedes comprobar la transformación sin montar esos sistemas alrededor.

element_inventory.current_content: Idempotencia significa que aplicar la función dos veces da lo mismo que aplicarla una: f(f(x)) == f(x)...
element_inventory.attack: Could falsely universalize idempotence.
element_inventory.defense: Context limits the property to the normalizers pursued in S05 and explains why retries make it useful.
element_inventory.improved_content: Sobre eso se apoya la propiedad que persigue la sección entera. Idempotencia significa que aplicar la función dos veces da lo mismo que aplicarla una: f(f(x)) == f(x). Suena a curiosidad matemática y es una necesidad operativa: los datos se reprocesan, los trabajos se reintentan, y una normalización que no es idempotente convierte cada reintento en un resultado distinto.
